paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this chapter: God doesn't leave His people guessing. He gives them a calendar and says, "These are My appointed feasts, the feasts of the LORD that you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies." (Leviticus 23:2) They're His, set at His times, and they're for gathering. A holy life isn't something you make up as you go, it's one where you stop and meet with God on purpose.

Now look at what keeps showing up in those days: there's rest, and there's bringing the first of the harvest to God before anyone eats from it (Leviticus 23:14). There's humbling yourself on the Day of Atonement, "when atonement is made for you before the LORD your God." (Leviticus 23:28) And right in the middle, God says to leave the edges of the field for "the poor and the foreign resident." (Leviticus 23:22) So the feasts weren't only about what Israel did for God, they were about what God did for them, and how that should spill over onto other people.

Then God ends on joy: "you are to rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days." (Leviticus 23:40) He also has them dwell in booths "so that your descendants may know that I made the Israelites dwell in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt." (Leviticus 23:43) Friend, God wants His people to remember what He's done, and He wants them to be glad about it. So here's your takeaway: make room in your week to rest, to remember and to rejoice with God, and I'll be over here with the ovens warm, cheering you on.
